newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Deutsche tightens funds, probe continues.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Deutsche tightens funds, probe continues.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG on Friday vowed to tighten controls at its troubled British fund management business as investigators dissected the trading accounts of three British funds and more investors dumped their holdings.
Senior Deutsche Bank officials announced an overhaul of the supervision at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
"We are pushing for substantial improvements in internal controls," said Rolf Breuer, the Deutsche Bank director responsible for global fund management.
Trading in three funds managed by MGAM was temporarily halted this week due to "suspected irregularities."

The manager of two of the funds, Peter Young, has been suspended and his personal assets frozen pending a probe into his management of the funds, which held a high proportion of unlisted, speculative high-technology stocks.
Worried investors sold off eight percent of the funds worth 1.14 billion stg when trading resumed on Thursday and a further five percent on Friday.

Deutsche Bank, which has stepped into the rescue with a 180 million stg bail-out to remove the unlisted securities from the funds, is now considering putting MGAM under tighter control from Frankfurt.
An enforcement team from the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation, IMRO, is also carrying out a detailed dissection of MGAM's trading history.
The team of six was "...looking at every trade done by every fund manager," said one funds industry source.
No criminal charges have been brought, but the IMRO funds industry watchdog has said it is in touch with Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO).

Problems at the three funds came to light after it was discovered that Young had exceeded the maximum 10 percent limit on holdings of unlisted stocks and he was ordered to reduce these to five percent.

Rather than reduce the holdings, however, Young is alleged by Morgan Grenfell to have set up more unlisted holding companies in which to place some of the original shares, according to remarks attributed to the investment bank in London's Financial Times newspaper.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell spokesman Markus Will told Reuters on Friday the bank had issued an injuction against Young and is seeking to determine if he was personally linked to some of the holding companies held in the fund's portfolio.
"We injuncted Mr Peter Young since we suspected that he may have connections to some of the holding companies he had held in his portfolio," Will said.
Attempts by Reuters to contact Young on Friday to comment on the Morgan Grenfell statement were unsuccessful.
In Frankfurt and London, senior officials from both Deutsche Bank and investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell admitted to a breakdown of controls and supervision.

Amid reports that Deutsche might put its London funds management business under tighter Frankfurt control, Breuer said Deutsche was also reviewing whether or not MGAM's investment philosophy suited Deutsche Bank's rather more conservative approach.

In the conservative world of fund management the practice of holding a high proportion of unlisted assets is frowned on not only because they are often high-risk, but because they are difficult to value and to sell due to an often illiquid market.

Investigations into the affairs of MGAM have revealed the extent of holdings the funds had in speculative Scandinavian stocks, such as Swedish development company Sintercast, whose shares have come under selling pressure since the news broke.
Morgan Grenfell on Friday said its three funds under investigation could have holdings in Sintercast representing 58 percent of its voting rights.
Deutsche and MGAM also own a majority in Norwegian software house Sysdeco Group ASA, but Deutsche said neither of the banks planned to take the company over.(1=.6385 Pound)
